column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

“Whoever relieves a believer of one of the distresses of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the distresses of the Day of Resurrection; whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter;
whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim, Allah will conceal [his faults] in this world and the Hereafter. Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.

Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise. No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, except that tranquillity descends upon them, mercy covers them,

the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. And whoever is held back by his deeds will not be hastened forward by his lineage.” Reported by Muslim with this wording.
Naffasa (“relieves”): removes and dispels.
Kurbah (“distress”): great hardship; what troubles the soul and grieves the heart.
“Whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship”: by granting him respite until he is at ease, by giving him what removes his hardship, or by remitting [the debt] if he is his creditor.
“Allah will make things easy for him”: his affairs and what he seeks.
“Whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim”: one not known for harm or corruption, in that he knows that he committed a sin in the past and does not tell anyone of it.
“Allah will conceal [his faults] in this world and the Hereafter”: by not punishing him for what he committed.
“Whoever takes a path”: by walking on foot to gatherings of knowledge; it also covers the figurative path, such as memorising, revising, reading and seeking to understand.
Yaltamisu (“seeking”): looking for.
ʿIlman (“knowledge”): of the Sharīʿah, intending by it the Face of Allah the Exalted.

“Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise”: by making easy for him the knowledge he sought and acting on what it requires, or other knowledge that leads him to Paradise. It may also mean making easy the physical path to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, which is the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ).
“One of the houses of Allah”: the mosques.
Al-sakīnah (“tranquillity”): calm and dignity.
“Mercy covers them”: enfolds them from every side.
“The angels surround them”: encircle them so that they leave the devil no gap through which to reach those remembering [Allah].
“And Allah mentions them”: praises them,
“among those who are with Him”: of the angels.
Baṭṭaʾa (“is held back”): falls short, through the lack of some conditions of validity or completeness.
“Will not be hastened forward by his lineage”: it will not bring him to the ranks of those with complete deeds, because one hastens to happiness by deeds, not by noble descent.
The virtue of meeting the needs of the Muslims and benefiting them with whatever one can of knowledge,
standing, wealth, a word of advice, counsel, directing to good, helping oneself or through intercession, or supplicating for them in their absence.
Encouragement to make things easy for one in hardship.

The hadiths on its virtue are many, among them the report of Muslim: “Whoever would be pleased that Allah the Exalted save him from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection, let him relieve one in hardship or remit [his debt].”
Encouragement to conceal the faults of a Muslim who is not known for corruption. As for one known [for it], who does not care what he commits or what is said to him, his faults are not concealed;

rather, his case is raised to the one in authority, if no harm is feared from that, because concealing it would make him exceed all bounds in corruption and violating what is sacred, and embolden others to do as he does.
All of this concerns a sin that is over. As for one he sees still engaged in a sin, he must hasten to oppose it
and prevent him from it, if he is able to; delay is not permissible. If he is unable, he must raise the matter to the one in authority, if no harm would result.
When a servant resolves to help his brother, he should not be too cowardly to carry out his word and declare the truth, believing that Allah the Exalted is helping him.
The virtue of occupying oneself with seeking knowledge.
Urging people to gather to recite the Qurʾān in the mosques.
Allah has made the recompense depend on deeds, not on lineage.
The recompense is sometimes of the same kind as the deed.
